HOLD/cash are decision-economics comparators; unchanged price is a level comparator, not a fabricated directional hit rate. Paired directional divergence is differing issued directions divided by admitted comparable pairs. Accuracy lift is model accuracy minus baseline accuracy in percentage points. Preserve original disagreements and negative memory; do not select an ex-post winning baseline, feature set or cohort.

Economic false-positive early-exit opportunity cost and false-negative missed-drawdown cost require originally eligible, timely counterfactuals. The unit is the original frozen valuation currency, or an explicitly frozen percentage of starting wealth—not an assumed notional. Net utility is the paired difference in net liquidatable wealth after all applicable friction. Without those inputs every monetary result is UNKNOWN. Knowledge-time sensitivity requires original-versus-revised vintages or authenticated clock alternatives; no numerical revision-sensitivity estimate is available here. Descriptive daily drift and 7/14-day concerns cannot certify lift, independence, calibration or trading edge. No issued probability series is supplied for probability-calibration scoring.

Those are coverage/design floors, not a guarantee of independent information, power or economic value. No production/model promotion follows without applicable PIT proof, untouched forward evidence, independent review, replication and confirmed incremental net decision value. A separately authorized metadata-only correction would not itself establish any of those scientific claims. If an existing route already satisfies the relevant test, retain the no-new-code baseline and close that candidate. Only a separately authorized, nonduplicate metadata repair could proceed through its existing owner route; the bounded sequence would be original diff, exact-head deterministic positive/adversarial tests, independent review, then an ordinary scheduled source-to-due-outcome-to-adjudicator-to-Supervisor/Strategist run and actual S1 advisory readback.
